data.description:
Board request via DM (chat msg 59, human:forrest): "I think we need query string to keep page context in here. also, the lattice events should link to the lattice site" — this task is the second half (lattice events link to the lattice site); the query-string half is AS-9.

Interpretation decision (Owen, 2026-08-30): 'the lattice site' = the read-only web dashboard that ships with the Lattice CLI — 'lattice dashboard', default http://127.0.0.1:8799 — which supports per-task deep links via hash routes: #/task/<full-task-id>. No other lattice-viewing surface exists (nothing hosted, nothing in-repo). The chat server already resolves AS-n short codes to full task IDs (lib/lattice.js resolveShortId → taskId), so the link is <base>/#/task/<taskId>.

Scope: AS-n refs in chat messages — at minimum in #lattice-events system messages, sensibly everywhere refs render — gain a working hyperlink to the dashboard task page. Keep the existing in-app task panel (title/status hover context is good); add an 'open in Lattice' link there too. Dashboard base URL configurable (env var, e.g. LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL, default http://127.0.0.1:8799) since the port is a dashboard default, not a contract. Key files: apps/chat/public/app.js (bodyNode, showTaskPanel), apps/chat/server.js (pass base URL or expose in task payload).

Caveat on record: the link only resolves while 'lattice dashboard' is running locally. Planner may scope in having compose.yaml (or docs) bring the dashboard up alongside chat, or leave that as a follow-up. Rejected alternative: linking to task files on the GitHub remote (https://github.com/malls/american-software) — works without a running dashboard but lands on raw event logs/snapshots, not a task view; revisit only if the board prefers a zero-infrastructure target.
data.title: Chat: AS-n refs and lattice events link out to the Lattice dashboard (#/task/<id>)

data.body: Plan written (plans/task_01M18DNFKVP22J5PRW7EZ89J95.md, commit 6bd1780 on feat/AS-10-lattice-links). Key calls: (1) no new resolution machinery — refs already carry taskId in every message payload; add a url field in resolveShortId built from LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8799); (2) bodyNode anchors get real href/target=_blank/rel=noopener — plain click keeps the in-app task panel, modified click goes to the dashboard; panel gains 'Open in Lattice'; (3) compose decision: dashboard stays host-run, document-only — vendor tooling like git/sqlite3, containerizing removes nothing; dead links while it is down are accepted and documented. ~25 LOC + tests + README. Ready for the implementation sub-agent.

Implementation done (commit fe5e690, branch feat/AS-10-lattice-links). Built: resolveShortId adds url=<base>/#/task/<taskId> for exists:true (LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL env, default http://127.0.0.1:8799, trailing-slash trim, empty=unset); bodyNode anchors get real href + target=_blank rel=noopener with modified-click fallthrough (plain click keeps in-app panel); showTaskPanel adds 'Open in Lattice' anchor; compose passthrough (server env moved map->list form, compose requires one form); README config row + AS-10 section. Tested: 53/53 in-container (was 52; one new test). Hand-walk: /api/task and #lattice-events refs carry the url; AS-999 has none; LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL=:9999 override + revert verified live; lattice dashboard served 200 on :8799, connection-refused after stop with href unchanged (dead-by-design). One deviation: test/api.test.js also had a deepEqual on the /api/task payload — updated it (plan named only lattice.test.js). QA attack points: (1) real-browser click semantics — plain vs cmd/ctrl/shift/middle click on a ref (criteria 4), I verified code paths not clicks; (2) devtools check of rendered anchor attrs (criterion 2); (3) 'Open in Lattice' visual placement in the task panel — unstyled anchor, class lattice-open, no CSS added.

REVIEW (qa-priya, cold, branch feat/AS-10-lattice-links @ fe5e690): PASS — no rework, no inline fixes. Suite: ran docker compose run --rm --build test myself — 53/53 pass (claim verified). Criteria: (1) PASS, in-container run incl. new dashboardTaskUrl/url cases; (2) PASS code-trace+API — bodyNode sets href from ref.url, target=_blank, rel=noopener; live /api/task/AS-10 returns url=http://127.0.0.1:8799/#/task/task_01M18DNF... (no browser devtools session — anchor attrs verified in code, url value verified over HTTP); (3) PASS API-level — all 45 #lattice-events messages carry refs with correct url, same bodyNode path; (4) PASS code-trace — plain click preventDefault→showTaskPanel; modified-click guard (meta/ctrl/shift/alt/button===1) falls through to real href (note: middle-click fires auxclick in modern browsers, so browser default covers it regardless — guard is harmless belt-and-braces); (5) PASS code-trace+API — 'Open in Lattice ↗' anchor only in exists branch; 'No such task.' branch unchanged; (6) PASS live — /api/task/AS-999 → {exists:false}, no url key; bodyNode filters !exists refs before any anchor is created → plain text; (7) PASS unit+compose-config — env override + trailing-slash trim covered in passing in-container tests; LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL=http://probe:1234 docker compose config shows passthrough, unset shows null with CHAT_BIND preserved (map→list conversion dropped nothing; cli/test services untouched); (8) PASS curl-level — started host lattice dashboard: GET / → 200 (SPA, hash route client-side); stopped it: connection refused, hrefs unaffected (server-rendered from env) — actual click-through is code-trace, honest level as on AS-9. (9) PASS — README config row + 'Links to Lattice (AS-10)' section w/ host-run decision. Attack pass: zero innerHTML (grep), el() is textContent-only, title/href set as DOM properties — hostile task titles inert; href built server-side from taskId only, never title. Hostile LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL (javascript: scheme) would flow to href — accepted trust boundary: operator-set server env, same trust level as compose.yaml itself; noting for the record, not a blocker. Deviation (api.test.js deepEqual) reviewed: justified, plan omission. Non-blocking nit: comments in lib/test say compose passthrough sets '' when host var is absent — compose actually omits the var (config renders null); the ||-default handles both, and ''-as-unset is still right for hand-exported empties, so behavior is correct — comment attribution only. Recommendation: done.
